architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalization.basis: selected_candidate_id was null; a decision naming no candidate is an abstention

acceptance_criterion.claim: The uncertainty probe is complete only when a subsequent full-coverage performance experiment can distinguish temporal hold-drift mitigation from viscosity-scale or process-state change.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Pass the pre-experiment gate only if AC1920 and TK100 reactive contributions are documented, true NCO:OH stoichiometry is recalculated, conditioning/loading/reaction history/sample age and state-anchor timing are frozen, matched E5 reference replicates are defined, and quantitative pre-result bounds are recorded for initial viscosity, state-calibrated viscosity, 80-130 C response deviation, and replicate/process-state variability. Otherwise do not adjudicate S1C40 or any alternative as an interpretable performance result.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: The probe fails if functionality or stoichiometry cannot be verified, process/state controls cannot be frozen, the E5 reference distribution cannot be defined, or quantitative acceptance bounds cannot be specified before physical adjudication.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: After the gate: 80-130 C temperature sweeps with replicates and an in-range 120 C state anchor, plus matched 120 C hold measurements at 15, 60, and 90 min.

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Provisional full-coverage performance candidate: 15 wt% acrylic-like modifier plus 2.5 wt% minor-tackifier-like modifier on the E2 core. It is not frozen because reactive functionality, true stoichiometry, process history, state-anchor definition, and quantitative viscosity acceptance bounds remain unresolved.
Full-coverage robustness alternative with 5 wt% tackifier-like modifier; higher justified modifier burden and greater risk of viscosity-scale or processability shifts than S1C40.
Lower-burden full-coverage alternative, but its 12.5 wt% acrylic-like level has weaker support and may produce an effect too small to distinguish from E2 state variation.
Low-burden tackifier-only mechanistic control; inappropriate as the default performance-mitigation experiment because it zeroes an independently supported acrylic-like axis.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The primary failure mode is thermal-hold viscosity drift, so the next performance experiment must directly measure the matched 120 C hold rather than optimize nominal viscosity. The local experiments establish the E5-versus-E1 hold contrast, monotonic 80-130 C thermal response, and large E2 realization-state spread. The state-aware rheology rules indicate that a new realization requires an in-range state anchor and that static viscosity, thermal response, and temporal drift are separate coordinates. Curated PUR literature supports acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like formulation families and broad regions, but it is analogue guidance rather than a predictor of the held-out wet-lab result; the approximately 15 wt% acrylic evidence is directional/noncommensurate, while approximately 20-25 wt% are the more directly commensurate coarse anchors and approximately 5 wt% is the repeated minor-tackifier region. Conservative design constraints require full coverage of both independently supported axes for performance mitigation, bounded modifier loading, matched process history, and a falsifiable hold-window test. S1C40 remains the provisional performance candidate, with S1C41 as the nearby higher-tackifier robustness alternative, but the Skeptic's objections remain material: SI thresholds are not evidence-derived, usable viscosity and temperature-response fidelity are undefined, and a single-realization E5 comparison is underspecified. The Robustness Adjudicator therefore correctly changes the immediate decision to an uncertainty probe. Before freezing a candidate, verify AC1920 and TK100 functionality and recalculate true NCO:OH stoichiometry, freeze process and state-anchor procedures, define quantitative viscosity and response bounds, and establish the matched E5 reference distribution. This does not remove the supported secondary modifier axis; it gates the full mitigation experiment until it can be interpreted.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: Required canonical bridge before candidate ranking. This will establish the formulation-only versus state-aware interpretation, state-shift master-curve structure, need for state calibration, local apparent temperature sensitivity, and the design-rule distinction between thermal response and temporal hold stability.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After the local objective and failure mode are established, retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, original E2 reactive-core anchor, independently supported acrylic and tackifier axes, and the historical or claim boundary before comparing candidate formulations.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Thermal-hold stability at 120 C over the measured 15-90 min window, using SI and absolute drift.
Initial and anchor-temperature viscosity level within measured support, without inventing units or extrapolating beyond the supplied measurements.
Temperature-response shape and apparent temperature sensitivity over 80-130 C.
Repeatability and realization/process-state risk, including whether the candidate requires state calibration.
Stoichiometric and process feasibility of retaining the reactive-core anchor while adding modifier axes.
Evidence commensurability: direct numeric anchors versus directional analogue evidence versus conservative extrapolation bounds.
Whether acrylic and tackifier effects are independently supported and whether their combination remains inside the bounded candidate lattice.
Information value for distinguishing improved hold stability from an apparent viscosity shift or altered process state.
counterfactual_checks: Would the candidate still be preferred if the nominal viscosity level were held constant and only thermal-hold drift were compared?
Would the apparent improvement persist after accounting for state calibration and replicate/process-history variation?
Is the improvement attributable to reduced temporal drift rather than simply selecting a different temperature-response curve?
Would an E2 reactive-core-only or single-axis comparator be needed to test whether the multi-component intervention adds value?
Does the candidate remain feasible if the external acrylic percentage is treated as a directional analogue rather than an exact local formulation percentage?
Would the candidate still be acceptable if judged over the full measured 80-130 C range rather than at one nominal temperature?
Could a change in modifier functionality or stoichiometric balance explain the result without claiming a molecular mechanism from rheology alone?
planner.decision_goal: Select one pre-result candidate experiment intended to mitigate thermal-hold viscosity drift while preserving a usable viscosity level and temperature response within the measured operating domain.
design_implications: Use performance mitigation rather than single-factor causal isolation because the hold-drift failure is already established and the immediate objective is to reduce it.
Do not rank candidates using nominal viscosity alone; jointly evaluate viscosity level, temperature sensitivity, thermal-hold drift, and repeatability or process-state risk.
Prefer candidate interventions whose active modifier axes are independently supported by the supplied evidence and whose combined loading remains within the bounded candidate lattice.
Treat the acrylic anchors near 15-25 wt% as directly usable only as coarse, noncommensurate formulation-family guidance; do not convert them into an exact total-formulation optimum.
Treat the minor tackifier guidance below about 10 wt% as a conservative extrapolation limit rather than a measured local target.
Preserve the original E2 reactive-core anchor unless the evidence-derived candidate hypothesis provides a bounded and explicitly justified formulation-family change.
Use the state-aware summary to determine whether one-point state calibration is required and whether the next experiment must emphasize thermal response, temporal hold response, or both.
Keep stoichiometry, process history, modifier functionality, and realization state explicit because rheology alone cannot establish a molecular mechanism.
material_regularities_to_use: All available temperature sweeps for E1, E2, and E3 decrease monotonically from 80 to 130 C, so temperature response must be evaluated separately from absolute viscosity level.
The measured temperature support is 80-130 C; candidate assessment should avoid unsupported temperature extrapolation.

E2 has large descriptive run spread, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios approximately 2.8-3.6 across 80-130 C, indicating that realization or process state may materially affect apparent viscosity.
E1 and E5 provide a direct original-system thermal-hold contrast at 120 C over 15-90 min, establishing hold drift as distinct from the temperature-sweep response.
The supplied external evidence supports acrylic and minor-tackifier formulation families only as priors and directional design guidance, not as proof of a local optimum.
The state-shift master-curve, state-calibration, and thermal-versus-temporal response implications must be taken from the upstream state-aware rheology summary before candidate ranking.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold stability is the established primary failure mode: E5 shows large viscosity drift at 120 C (SI=0.515 from 15 to 60 min and 0.931 from 15 to 90 min), whereas E1 is comparatively stable (SI=0.095 and 0.168). Nominal viscosity alone is insufficient because E2 also exhibits substantial realization/process-state spread across nominal temperature sweeps.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep over 80-130 C with an anchor temperature inside measured support.
Replicate temperature sweeps sufficient to quantify nominal run spread and distinguish material response from realization/process-state variation.
Thermal-hold trajectory at 120 C sampled at 15, 60, and 90 min, or the same frozen measured window used for the original comparison.
Initial viscosity and time-resolved viscosity during the hold, retaining source units and calculating SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0.
Process-history, conditioning, loading, and stoichiometric records needed to interpret state variation.
If required by the state-aware summary, a one-point state calibration measurement paired with the temperature sweep.
A frozen pre-result candidate definition and adjudication criteria covering viscosity, temperature response, hold stability, repeatability, feasibility, and out-of-domain status.
uncertainty_triggers: The state-aware summary indicates a substantial state shift or that formulation-only temperature modeling is inadequate.
A candidate lies outside the 80-130 C temperature support or outside the measured 15-90 min hold window.
Candidate performance depends on an acrylic or tackifier level beyond the evidence-bounded lattice.
Modifier functionality, hydroxyl content, molecular weight, catalyst, or process history differs materially from the local system.
A single nominal viscosity appears favorable but replicate spread remains comparable to or larger than the candidate-to-candidate difference.
The candidate changes multiple axes without independent support for each active modifier axis.
Hold drift improves but the temperature response or processability becomes unsupported or infeasible.
Available evidence is only directional or noncommensurate and is being used as though it were a directly comparable numeric anchor.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate mitigates thermal-hold viscosity drift without relying on a static-viscosity shift or losing the supported local temperature-response behavior.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Under matched process conditions, the candidate must show lower median SI than the unstable E5 reference in the 15-60 min window, with a prespecified practical target of SI <= 0.30, and should remain below SI=0.60 over 15-90 min; its 80-130 C viscosity curve must remain monotonically decreasing and its replicate spread must be reported rather than treated as material response.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Failure is declared if the candidate does not reduce drift relative to the matched E5 reference, if apparent improvement disappears after state calibration, if replicate/process-state variation is comparable to the claimed improvement, or if the temperature response becomes non-monotonic or unsupported within 80-130 C.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C hold at 15, 60, and 90 min, with 80-130 C temperature sweeps and an in-range 120 C state anchor.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Matched 120 C thermal-hold viscosity trajectory with viscosity recorded at 15, 60, and 90 min and SI calculated as (eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0; jointly report initial viscosity, 80-130 C temperature response, replicate spread, and state-calibrated comparisons.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Control conditioning, loading, reaction history, sample age, and measurement protocol. Perform replicate sweeps and one in-range state-specific viscosity anchor at 120 C for each new formulation or realization, using that anchor to locate the realization on the transferable local thermal-response shape.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: Temperature sweep over 80-130 C plus matched 120 C hold at 15, 60, and 90 min; use the 15-60 min interval as the primary directly comparable window and 15-90 min as a secondary persistence window.

evidence_against: The external acrylic and tackifier evidence uses different chemistries, functionality, catalysts, and process histories.
The candidate changes two axes simultaneously, so it is not a single-factor causal-isolation experiment.
Major process-history fields are missing, creating realization-state uncertainty.
evidence_for: Covers both independently supported axes: 15 wt% acrylic-like modifier and 2.5 wt% minor tackifier-like modifier.
Preserves the E2 reactive-core proportions and is within the bounded modifier lattice.

The acrylic level is directly aligned with the externally supported 15 wt% lower-region evidence, while the tackifier level is a conservative minor perturbation below the repeatedly documented approximately 5 wt% cluster.

External support is analogue or comparative, not a local property prediction; local support comes from the established E5 hold failure, E2 state variability, and the requirement to test drift directly.

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E5 shows strong 120 C hold drift, with SI=0.515 from 15 to 60 min and SI=0.931 from 15 to 90 min, while E1 is comparatively stable.
Measured local evidence: all available E1-E3 temperature sweeps decrease monotonically from 80 to 130 C, so static viscosity and temperature response must be separated from temporal hold stability.
Measured local evidence: E2 has substantial realization/process-state spread, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios approximately 2.8-3.6.

Derived physical/model rule: local realization state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a shared thermal-response shape remains transferable; one in-range state anchor is therefore required for a new realization.
Derived physical/model rule: thermal-hold drift is a separate response coordinate and cannot be inferred from static viscosity.

External analogue evidence: acrylic-like modifiers are supported directionally across approximately 15-25 wt%, with directly commensurate coarse anchors near 20% and 25%, but without proof of a local optimum.
External analogue evidence: minor tackifier-like modifiers are repeatedly represented near 5 wt%, with below-about-10 wt% guidance as a conservative upper bound.
Conservative design principle: for performance mitigation, both independently supported intervention axes must be covered before minimum modifier burden is considered.
Unresolved uncertainty: modifier functionality, reactive-group density, process history, and realization state are not established for the local system.
proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate the established 120 C thermal-hold viscosity drift while preserving a usable viscosity level and the measured 80-130 C decreasing temperature response. The local diagnosis supports an E2-centered state-aware test; external formulation evidence supports testing both acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes as a bounded formulation family, not an exact optimum.
unresolved_questions: What are the verified reactive-group contents and effective stoichiometric contributions of AC1920 and TK100?
Can process history, conditioning, loading, reaction temperature, reaction time, and sample age be matched tightly enough to separate formulation effects from state shifts?
Does the full-coverage intervention improve hold stability at comparable calibrated viscosity, rather than merely changing the viscosity scale?
Is the supported region a broad formulation family rather than a single optimal composition?
Does increasing tackifier from 2.5 to 5 wt% provide incremental stability benefit over the lower-burden S1C40 condition?
Are the local acceptance thresholds appropriate after replicate variance and state-calibration uncertainty are quantified?

required_conditions: Verify AC1920 and TK100 functionality, reactive-group content, and recalculate true NCO:OH stoichiometry before experimentation.
Freeze conditioning, loading, reaction history, sample age, and the state-anchor timing and normalization procedure.
Use matched E5 reference replicates or a prespecified reference distribution rather than an ambiguous single-realization comparison.
Prespecify acceptable initial and state-calibrated viscosity bounds, temperature-response deviation over 80-130 C, and replicate/process-state variability.
Label SI <= 0.30 and SI < 0.60 as conservative prospective design thresholds unless a traceable pre-result basis is supplied.
Interpret S1C40 as a dual-axis performance test only; attribution to either modifier axis requires matched single-axis controls.
Retain S1C41 as the preferred nearby robustness alternative if the uncertainty probe favors the repeated approximately 5% tackifier region.

robustness_checks.detail: S1C40 directly tests the established 120 C thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure while preserving the E2 reactive-core proportions and the required 80-130 C temperature-response assessment.
The declared intent is performance_mitigation, so a dual-axis intervention is appropriate; S1C40 covers both independently supported acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes.
S1C40 is the lowest-burden strong-evidence full-coverage candidate among the proposed primary options. Its rank is not based on burden alone and does not promote a partial-coverage candidate.

S1C40 remains a plausible supported-region test, but its 15% acrylic level is directional/noncommensurate rather than a directly commensurate anchor. S1C41 becomes a credible nearby alternative because its 5% tackifier level lies in the repeated minor-resin region.

The required state-anchor, replicate, process-history, and matched-hold measurements are specified, but missing process fields and unresolved modifier functionality or stoichiometric contributions could confound interpretation.

The measurement plan is directionally sufficient, but usable viscosity, allowable state-calibrated scale shift, temperature-response fidelity, and replicate-variability bounds are not quantitatively prespecified. SI thresholds must be labeled conservative design thresholds.

The unresolved stoichiometric feasibility and process-state uncertainty, together with underspecified acceptance bounds, are serious enough to require an uncertainty probe or pre-experiment gate before accepting the performance result as interpretable.

counterfactual_failures: The proposal does not fully specify whether S1C40 would remain preferred when candidates are compared at matched calibrated viscosity rather than nominal composition or initial viscosity.
The proposed SI criterion may still classify an apparent viscosity-scale shift as successful unless the state-calibrated trajectory comparison and acceptable scale range are numerically prespecified.

The proposal does not include a full-coverage lower-burden comparator such as S1C30 in the primary recommendation, although S1C30 has lower total modifier burden; excluding it is defensible only because its 10 wt% acrylic level lies below the supported acrylic band and has weaker evidence coverage.

A positive S1C40 result would not distinguish reduced temporal drift from changes in modifier functionality, stoichiometric balance, or realization state without the required process and material characterization.

critical_findings.evidence: The payload supplies E5 SI values of 0.515 and 0.931, but no evidence-derived threshold of 0.30. The criterion is presented as a prespecified target without labeling it clearly as a conservative design principle.
critical_findings.issue: The proposed SI <= 0.30 practical target is not traceable to a supplied local measurement or directly commensurate external anchor.

critical_findings.evidence: The decision goal requires preserving a usable viscosity level and measured 80-130 C response, but the criterion only requires monotonic decrease and reports initial viscosity. 'Usable' and acceptable calibrated viscosity deviation remain vague and could be adjudicated post hoc.
critical_findings.issue: The acceptance criterion does not define a quantitative usable-viscosity or temperature-response fidelity boundary.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate hypothesis states that the reported 15% acrylic addition has an unverified denominator and is retained only as provisional noncommensurate evidence; directly commensurate coarse anchors are approximately 20% and 25%.
critical_findings.issue: The phrase 'directly aligned with the externally supported 15 wt% lower-region evidence' overstates the commensurability of the acrylic anchor.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate hypothesis explicitly states that AC1920 or TK100 may contribute reactive hydroxyl or other NCO-reactive groups and that true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified specifications. The proposal acknowledges this uncertainty but does not make verification a pre-experiment gate.
critical_findings.issue: Reactive stoichiometric feasibility is not resolved before treating S1C40 as preserving the E2 reactive-core anchor.

critical_findings.evidence: The two candidates differ in tackifier loading and consequently in normalized reactive-core fractions; without a matched no-tackifier acrylic comparator, the incremental tackifier effect remains unresolved. This is acceptable for the stated performance objective but should not be interpreted causally.
critical_findings.issue: The comparison of S1C40 with S1C41 is informative for tackifier loading but does not establish that the tackifier axis contributes independently to hold stability.

critical_findings.evidence: The supplied state-aware summary reports E5 hold trajectories but does not establish a replicate distribution for E5. A median candidate SI should be compared against a prespecified reference value or matched E5 replicate distribution, not an ambiguously defined single-reference median.
critical_findings.issue: The phrase 'lower median SI than the unstable E5 reference' is statistically underspecified if E5 has only one original realization.

interpretability_failures: No explicit quantitative acceptance interval is provided for initial or state-calibrated viscosity, so improvement could be claimed despite an unacceptable viscosity-scale shift.
No explicit quantitative criterion is provided for preserving the local thermal-response shape beyond monotonicity; a substantially altered but still monotonic curve could pass.
S1C40 changes two modifier axes, so any positive result cannot support an independent acrylic or tackifier causal claim.
Reactive-group content, stoichiometric contribution, and process-history fields remain unresolved and could confound formulation effects with realization state.
The state-anchor timing and definition should be frozen explicitly, including whether the anchor is measured before the hold, at 15 minutes, or by another standardized condition.

leakage_check.detail: The supplied payload states that validation formulation identity and wet-lab outcome were not visible to the state-aware tool and were excluded from candidate construction, ranking, and tie-breaking. The historical note that the exact V2 grid and refinement software were formalized after validation creates provenance risk, but no validation identity, outcome, or outcome-derived label is evident in this proposal.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly prioritizes the established thermal-hold failure, uses the state-aware rheology interpretation, separates static viscosity from temperature response and temporal drift, and requires full coverage of both independently supported modifier axes for a performance-mitigation experiment. However, its 'minimum-burden' wording is only defensible within the strong-evidence full-coverage subset, and the 15 wt% acrylic rationale should not be described as directly commensurate because that percentage is explicitly noncommensurate and directional.

required_corrections: Retain S1C40 as the provisional performance candidate, but state explicitly that its rank is among strong-evidence, full-coverage candidates rather than a global minimum-modifier solution.
Recast the 15 wt% acrylic support as directional/noncommensurate evidence and identify approximately 20% and 25% as the directly commensurate coarse anchors.
Label SI <= 0.30 and SI < 0.60 as conservative prospective design thresholds, or provide a traceable pre-result basis for them.
Predefine quantitative bounds for acceptable initial and state-calibrated viscosity, temperature-response deviation over 80-130 C, and replicate/process-state variability.
Verify AC1920 and TK100 functionality and recalculate NCO:OH stoichiometry before experimentation; do not claim preservation of the E2 reactive-core anchor until this is completed.
Define the state-anchor timing and normalization procedure before the hold, and specify how the candidate SI distribution will be compared with the E5 reference.
State explicitly that S1C40 is a performance-mitigation test and that any attribution to either modifier axis requires additional matched controls.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects the boundary between measured local evidence, state-aware rheological rules, external analogue evidence, and conservative design principles. It correctly avoids claiming a local optimum or molecular mechanism. Boundary clarity is weakened by treating the 15 wt% acrylic literature value as more commensurate than the payload permits and by presenting SI <= 0.30 as a practical target without explicitly labeling it as a conservative design rule.

tool_trace.reason: Required canonical bridge before candidate ranking. claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a low-complexity common thermal-response shape remains transferable.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
